meta.description: Import and normalise customer, account, card, and transaction data from a branch migration export file into the CardDemo system's target data stores.
meta.process_description: CBIMPORT is the counterpart to CBEXPORT: it reads a structured, multi-record-type migration file produced by a source branch and splits it into five separate, normalised output files (Customer, Account, Card Cross-Reference, Card, and Transaction). Each record in the input file carries a type indicator ('C', 'A', 'X', 'D', 'T') that determines which target file it is routed to, with all relevant fields mapped and written accordingly. The program validates data integrity using checksums and tracks import statistics (records read and written per entity type) throughout the run. Any records with unrecognised record types are flagged and written to a dedicated error report file, ensuring a clean and auditable migration outcome.

files.EXPFILE: Source branch migration export file containing all customer, account, card, cross-reference, and transaction records in a unified multi-record-type layout
files.CUSTOUT: Target customer master file receiving normalised customer profile records (personal details, address, SSN, FICO score, etc.)
files.ACCTOUT: Target account master file receiving normalised credit card account records (balance, credit limit, dates, status, etc.)
files.XREFOUT: Target card cross-reference file linking card numbers to customer and account identifiers
files.TRNXOUT: Target transaction history file receiving individual credit card transaction records
files.CARDOUT: Target card file receiving physical card records (card number, expiry, status, etc.)
files.ERROUT: Error report file capturing records that failed validation or carried an unrecognised record type, with timestamp and diagnostic message

business_rules: Each record in the migration file must carry a valid record type indicator ('C', 'A', 'X', 'T', or 'D'); records with any other type are rejected to the error file and counted separately to flag data quality issues.

All five output files (Customer, Account, Cross-Reference, Transaction, Card) must be successfully opened before processing begins; failure to open any file causes an immediate abnormal termination to prevent partial or corrupt imports.

Customer records must carry full personal identification data including SSN, government-issued ID, date of birth, FICO credit score, and primary card-holder indicator, preserving regulatory and credit risk information across the migration.

The card cross-reference record (type 'X') must link a card number to both a customer ID and an account ID, maintaining the three-way relationship that is essential for card authorisation and account servicing.
Data integrity is validated using checksums after processing to ensure the imported data matches the source export, supporting reconciliation and audit requirements for the branch migration.

Import statistics are tracked at the record-type level (customers, accounts, cross-references, transactions, cards, errors) to provide a full reconciliation count for sign-off by operations and the receiving branch.
Any write failure to any output file causes an immediate abnormal termination, preventing silent data loss or partial record sets that would compromise the integrity of the migrated portfolio.
The program records the date and time of the import run, providing an audit trail that ties the imported data to a specific migration event for regulatory and operational purposes.

lines.explanation: This is the top-level orchestration paragraph that drives the entire branch migration import run from start to finish. It sequences the four major business phases — setup, data routing, integrity validation, and closedown — ensuring a controlled, auditable import of all customer, account, card, and transaction records.
Initialises the import run: opens all output files, records the batch execution date and time, and zeroes all import counters before any data is processed.

Reads every record from the source branch migration file and routes each one to the correct target file (customer, account, card, cross-reference, or transaction) based on its record type, counting successes and rejections throughout.
Performs post-processing data integrity checks using checksums to confirm that the volume and content of imported records matches what the source branch exported, supporting reconciliation sign-off.
Closes all input and output files, writes the final import statistics summary, and completes the audit trail for the migration event.
Returns control to the operating system, signalling that the import batch job has completed.

This paragraph initialises the branch migration import job by capturing the exact date and time of execution for audit purposes, then opens all required input and output files before processing begins. It establishes the audit trail and ensures the system is fully ready to receive and route migrated customer, account, card, and transaction data.
Logs to the system console that the customer data import job has started, providing an operator-visible confirmation of job commencement.
Records the four-digit year of the import run into the audit timestamp, anchoring the migration event to a specific calendar year.
Inserts a hyphen separator between the year and month portions of the formatted import date for readability and standard date formatting.
Records the two-digit month of the import run into the audit timestamp, identifying the calendar month of the migration event.
Inserts a hyphen separator between the month and day portions of the formatted import date.
Records the two-digit day of the month of the import run into the audit timestamp, completing the full calendar date of the migration event.
Records the two-digit hour at which the import job started, establishing the precise time of the migration event for audit and reconciliation.
Inserts a colon separator between the hour and minute portions of the formatted import time.
Records the two-digit minute at which the import job started, refining the audit timestamp to sub-hour precision.
Inserts a colon separator between the minute and second portions of the formatted import time.
Records the two-digit second at which the import job started, completing the full time-of-day audit stamp for the migration run.
Opens all required input and output files (source export file, all five target data files, and the error report), ensuring the system is fully prepared before any records are processed.
Writes the formatted import date to the system console log, providing operators and auditors with a permanent record of when this migration batch was executed.
Writes the formatted import time to the system console log, completing the audit entry that ties all imported records to this specific migration event.

variables.name: EXPORT-INPUT-RECORD
variables.description: Raw 500-byte buffer that holds each record read from the branch migration export file before it is parsed and routed. Every customer, account, card, cross-reference, and transaction record arriving from the source branch passes through this buffer as the first step of the import process.

variables.name: ERROR-OUTPUT-RECORD
variables.description: 132-byte output buffer used to write a formatted diagnostic line to the error report file (ERROUT) whenever a migration record fails validation or carries an unrecognised record type. The 132-character width matches a standard print line, making the error report directly readable by operations staff during reconciliation.

variables.name: WS-FILE-STATUS-AREA
variables.description: Group record that consolidates the I/O status codes for every file involved in the migration import run. By grouping all file health indicators together, the program can quickly determine whether any input or output file has encountered an error and take immediate corrective action, such as aborting the run to prevent partial or corrupt data being written to the target system.

variables.name: WS-EXPORT-STATUS
variables.description: Two-character I/O status code returned by the operating system after each read operation on the branch migration export file (EXPFILE). The program inspects this code after every read to decide whether to continue processing, handle end-of-file, or abort due to a read error.

variables.name: WS-EXPORT-EOF
variables.description: Condition flag that becomes true when the migration export file has been fully read (file status '10' = end-of-file). When this condition is true, the program stops reading and moves on to closing files and printing the final reconciliation statistics.

variables.name: WS-EXPORT-OK
variables.description: Condition flag that confirms the last read from the branch migration export file completed successfully (file status '00' = no error). The program uses this to verify that each record was retrieved cleanly before attempting to parse and route it to the appropriate target file.

variables.name: WS-CUSTOMER-STATUS
variables.description: Two-character I/O status code returned after each write operation to the customer master output file (CUSTOUT). The program checks this after every customer record write to confirm the customer profile was stored successfully; a non-zero value triggers an immediate abnormal termination to prevent silent data loss.

variables.name: WS-CUSTOMER-OK
variables.description: Condition flag that confirms a customer profile record was written successfully to the customer master file (file status '00'). Only when this condition is true does the program increment the customer import counter and continue processing the next record.

variables.name: WS-ACCOUNT-STATUS
variables.description: Two-character I/O status code returned after each write operation to the account master output file (ACCTOUT). The program inspects this after every account record write to ensure credit card account data — including balances, credit limits, and dates — was persisted correctly.

variables.name: WS-ACCOUNT-OK
variables.description: Condition flag that confirms a credit card account record was written successfully to the account master file (file status '00'). The program relies on this condition before counting the account as successfully imported and moving to the next record.

variables.name: WS-XREF-STATUS
variables.description: Two-character I/O status code returned after each write to the card cross-reference output file (XREFOUT). The cross-reference links a card number to both a customer and an account, so any write failure here would break the three-way relationship essential for card authorisation and account servicing.

variables.name: WS-XREF-OK
variables.description: Condition flag that confirms a card-to-customer-to-account cross-reference record was written successfully (file status '00'). Only when this condition is true is the cross-reference counted as imported, preserving the integrity of the card authorisation linkage.

variables.name: WS-TRANSACTION-STATUS
variables.description: Two-character I/O status code returned after each write to the transaction history output file (TRNXOUT). The program checks this after every transaction write to ensure the customer's historical transaction data is being preserved accurately during the migration.

variables.name: WS-TRANSACTION-OK
variables.description: Condition flag that confirms a transaction history record was written successfully to the transaction output file (file status '00'). The program uses this to validate each transaction write before incrementing the transaction import counter.

variables.name: WS-CARD-STATUS
variables.description: Two-character I/O status code returned after each write to the physical card output file (CARDOUT). The program checks this to confirm that card details — including card number, expiry date, CVV, and active status — were stored correctly in the target system.

variables.name: WS-CARD-OK
variables.description: Condition flag that confirms a physical card record was written successfully to the card output file (file status '00'). Only when this condition is true does the program count the card as successfully migrated.

variables.name: WS-ERROR-STATUS
variables.description: Two-character I/O status code returned after each write to the error report file (ERROUT). The program checks this to confirm that rejected records and their diagnostic messages were successfully captured for operations review and reconciliation sign-off.

variables.name: WS-ERROR-OK
variables.description: Condition flag that confirms a rejected record's error entry was written successfully to the error report file (file status '00'). This ensures that every failed record is accounted for in the error log, supporting a complete and auditable reconciliation of the migration run.

variables.name: WS-IMPORT-CONTROL
variables.description: Group record that captures the date and time stamp of the import batch run. This information forms the audit trail that ties all imported records to a specific, identifiable migration event, satisfying regulatory and operational traceability requirements.

variables.name: WS-IMPORT-DATE
variables.description: Calendar date on which the branch migration import job was executed (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD). This date is recorded as part of the audit trail so that operations, compliance, and the receiving branch can identify exactly which business day the portfolio data was migrated.

variables.name: WS-IMPORT-TIME
variables.description: Wall-clock time at which the branch migration import job was executed (formatted as HH:MM:SS). Together with the import date, this provides a precise timestamp for the migration event, enabling operations to correlate the import run with system logs and reconciliation reports.

variables.name: WS-IMPORT-STATISTICS
variables.description: Group record that accumulates the record-level counts for the entire migration import run. These counters are the primary reconciliation tool: operations and the receiving branch use them to verify that every record from the source export file was either successfully imported into a target file or explicitly rejected to the error report, with no records silently lost.

variables.name: WS-TOTAL-RECORDS-READ
variables.description: Running total of all records read from the branch migration export file during the import run, regardless of record type or outcome. This is the control total against which all other counters (customers, accounts, cross-references, transactions, cards, and errors) must sum to confirm that no records were dropped during processing.

variables.name: WS-CUSTOMER-RECORDS-IMPORTED
variables.description: Count of customer profile records successfully written to the customer master file during this migration run. Operations and the receiving branch compare this figure against the expected number of customers in the source export to confirm that all customer personal, address, and credit risk data was migrated completely.

variables.name: WS-ACCOUNT-RECORDS-IMPORTED
variables.description: Count of credit card account records successfully written to the account master file during this migration run. This figure is used to verify that all account balances, credit limits, and status information from the source branch have been transferred to the receiving system without omission.

variables.name: WS-XREF-RECORDS-IMPORTED
variables.description: Count of card-to-customer-to-account cross-reference records successfully written to the cross-reference file during this migration run. Because each cross-reference record is essential for card authorisation and account servicing, this count must match the expected number of active cards in the migrated portfolio.

variables.name: WS-TRAN-RECORDS-IMPORTED
variables.description: Count of transaction history records successfully written to the transaction output file during this migration run. This figure allows operations to confirm that the full transaction history for all migrated accounts has been preserved, which is critical for customer statements, dispute resolution, and regulatory reporting.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RECORDS-IMPORTED
variables.description: Count of physical card records successfully written to the card output file during this migration run. Operations use this count to verify that all card numbers, expiry dates, CVV codes, and active statuses from the source branch have been migrated, ensuring cardholders can continue to use their cards without interruption.

variables.name: WS-ERROR-RECORDS-WRITTEN
variables.description: Count of records that failed validation and were written to the error report file during this migration run. This figure represents the volume of data that could not be automatically migrated and requires manual investigation and remediation by operations before the migration can be considered complete.

variables.name: WS-UNKNOWN-RECORD-TYPE-COUNT
variables.description: Count of records encountered in the migration export file that carried an unrecognised record type indicator (i.e., not 'C', 'A', 'X', 'T', or 'D'). A non-zero value signals a data quality problem in the source export — such as a corrupted file, a format mismatch, or an undocumented record type — that must be investigated before the migration can be signed off.

variables.name: WS-ERROR-RECORD
variables.description: Formatted error report line written to the error output file (ERROUT) for every record that fails validation or carries an unrecognised type. The structured layout — with pipe-delimited fields for timestamp, record type, sequence number, and diagnostic message — makes the error report human-readable for operations staff and machine-parseable for automated reconciliation tools.

variables.name: ERR-TIMESTAMP
variables.description: Date and time at which the rejected record was encountered during the import run, carried forward from the export file's own timestamp. This allows operations to pinpoint exactly when in the migration sequence a problem record appeared, aiding root-cause analysis and audit trail completeness.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Pipe character delimiter separating the timestamp from the record type in the error report line. This formatting character makes the error report easier for operations staff to read and allows automated tools to parse the fields reliably.

variables.name: ERR-RECORD-TYPE
variables.description: Single-character record type indicator copied from the rejected source record (e.g., 'C', 'A', 'X', 'T', 'D', or an unrecognised value). Including this in the error report allows operations to quickly categorise the nature of the failure — for example, distinguishing between a bad customer record and a completely unrecognised record type — and prioritise remediation accordingly.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Pipe character delimiter separating the record type from the sequence number in the error report line, maintaining consistent column formatting for readability and automated parsing.

variables.name: ERR-SEQUENCE
variables.description: Sequential position number of the rejected record within the migration export file. This allows operations to locate the exact record in the source file for manual inspection and correction, which is essential when remediating data quality issues before re-running the migration.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Pipe character delimiter separating the sequence number from the diagnostic message in the error report line, ensuring consistent formatting across all error entries for both human review and automated reconciliation processing.

variables.name: ERR-MESSAGE
variables.description: Plain-language diagnostic message describing why the record was rejected — for example, 'INVALID RECORD TYPE', 'MISSING SSN', or 'WRITE FAILURE ON CUSTOUT'. This message is the primary tool operations staff use to understand what went wrong with each rejected record and determine the corrective action needed before the migration can be completed.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: 43-byte padding of spaces that fills the remainder of the 132-character error report line after the diagnostic message. This ensures each error line is exactly the standard print-line width, preventing formatting issues when the error report is printed or displayed by operations tooling.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN-PROCESSING
paragraphs.description: This is the top-level orchestration paragraph that drives the entire branch migration import run from start to finish. It sequences the four major business phases — setup, data routing, integrity validation, and closedown — ensuring a controlled, auditable import of all customer, account, card, and transaction records.

paragraphs.name: 1000-INITIALIZE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph initialises the branch migration import job by capturing the exact date and time of execution for audit purposes, then opens all required input and output files before processing begins. It establishes the audit trail and ensures the system is fully ready to receive and route migrated customer, account, card, and transaction data.

paragraphs.name: 1100-OPEN-FILES
paragraphs.description: This paragraph prepares the migration import job for processing by opening all required data channels — the source export file for reading and all five normalised target files plus the error report for writing. If any single file cannot be opened, the job halts immediately to prevent a partial or corrupt import.

paragraphs.name: 2000-PROCESS-EXPORT-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the end-to-end processing of the branch migration export file, reading each incoming record in sequence and routing it to the appropriate target data store based on its record type. It acts as the central processing loop for the entire import run, ensuring every record in the source file is accounted for and handled.

paragraphs.name: 2100-READ-EXPORT-RECORD
paragraphs.description: Reads the next migration record from the source branch export file into the processing buffer. If the read fails for any reason other than reaching the end of the file, the program halts immediately to prevent corrupt or incomplete data from entering the target systems.

paragraphs.name: 2200-PROCESS-RECORD-BY-TYPE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph acts as the central routing hub of the import process, inspecting the record type indicator on each incoming migration record and directing it to the appropriate specialised processing routine. It ensures every record from the source branch export file is handled according to its entity type, with unrecognised records safely diverted to error handling.

paragraphs.name: 2300-PROCESS-CUSTOMER-RECORD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph normalises and writes a single customer profile record from the branch migration export into the CardDemo customer master file. It maps all personal, contact, identification, and credit risk fields from the source layout into the target structure, then persists the record and updates the running import count.

paragraphs.name: 2400-PROCESS-ACCOUNT-RECORD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph normalises and writes a single credit card account record from the branch migration export into the CardDemo target account master file. It maps all financial and administrative account attributes from the source layout to the target structure, then persists the record and updates the running import tally.

paragraphs.name: 2500-PROCESS-XREF-RECORD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph processes a card cross-reference record from the migration export file, establishing the critical three-way link between a physical card number, its owning customer, and the associated credit account in the target system. It writes this linkage to the cross-reference output file and terminates immediately if the write fails, ensuring no partial or missing card-to-customer-to-account relationships exist in the migrated portfolio.

paragraphs.name: 2600-PROCESS-TRAN-RECORD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph normalises and writes a single transaction history record from the branch migration export file into the CardDemo transaction data store. It maps all transaction details — including amount, merchant information, card linkage, and timestamps — to the target format, then persists the record and increments the running transaction import count.

paragraphs.name: 2650-PROCESS-CARD-RECORD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph transforms and persists a physical card record from the branch migration export into the CardDemo card master file. It maps all card-level attributes from the source data, writes the normalised record to the target file, and increments the running count of successfully migrated cards.

paragraphs.name: 2700-PROCESS-UNKNOWN-RECORD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles records from the migration export file that carry an unrecognised record type indicator, logging them as data quality exceptions and routing them to the error report to ensure the migration remains clean and fully auditable. It acts as a safety net, preventing corrupt or malformed source records from silently contaminating any of the five target data stores.

paragraphs.name: 2750-WRITE-ERROR
paragraphs.description: This paragraph writes a rejected or unrecognised record to the dedicated error report file, ensuring every data quality issue is captured and auditable. It also increments the running count of failed records to support end-of-run reconciliation and sign-off by operations.

paragraphs.name: 3000-VALIDATE-IMPORT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph represents the post-import data integrity validation checkpoint, confirming that all migrated records passed checksum and reconciliation checks. It signals to the operations team that the imported portfolio data is clean and ready for use in the CardDemo system.

paragraphs.name: 4000-FINALIZE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph concludes the branch migration import run by safely closing all data files and printing a full reconciliation summary to the job log, giving operations and the receiving branch a complete, auditable count of every record processed by entity type.

paragraphs.name: 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM
paragraphs.description: This paragraph performs an immediate, unrecoverable termination of the import job when a critical failure is detected, such as a file open error or a write failure to any output file. It ensures the migration is halted cleanly rather than continuing in a corrupted or partial state, protecting the integrity of the migrated portfolio.
